title: Topological Noetherianity after normalizing a base-point closure
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $f:X	o S$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $s\in S$. Give $Z_s=\overline{\{s\}}$ its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme], an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $
u_s:N_s=Z_s^
u	o Z_s\hookrightarrow S$ be its normalization in $\kappa(s)$ [def-sc-normalization, def-weil-residue-field]. Then the underlying Zariski topological space of $X	imes_SN_s$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is Noetherian: every nonempty collection of its closed subsets has a minimal member for inclusion. Neither excellence of $S$, finiteness of $
u_s$, nor Noetherianity of the local rings of $N_s$ is assumed.

source.place: Author draft, final sentences of the proof of Lemma 8.3.2, printed p. 18, finite-type alternative: application of [Hei73], W. Heinzer, Minimal primes of ideals and integral ring extensions, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 40 (1973), 370–372, to the normalization spectrum and its finite-type schemes. This asserts topological Noetherianity, not a finite normalization or a Noetherian normalization ring.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], $S$ has Noetherian underlying topology, and so does its closed subspace $Z_s$. Choose a finite affine open cover $S=\bigcup_i W_i$, $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, with $R_i$ Noetherian: [pqf-def-locnoeth] supplies such an affine cover and quasi-compactness supplies a finite subcover. Discard indices for which $U_i=Z_s\cap W_i$ is empty. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i/I_i)$. Since $Z_s$ is integral, [def-pc-integral-scheme] says $R_i/I_i$ is a domain, so $I_i=\mathfrak p_i$ is prime. Put $A_i=R_i/\mathfrak p_i$. It is Noetherian: the inverse image of any ideal $J\subseteq A_i$ is a finitely generated ideal of $R_i$, and the images of those generators generate $J$. Thus the finitely many $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ cover $Z_s$ by spectra of Noetherian domains.

source.place: Tag 01OV, definition-noetherian; Tag 01OZ, lemma-Noetherian-topology; affine quotient characterization of closed immersions, morphisms.tex Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion. The quotient-ring finite-generation argument is written out.

proof.text: The point $s$ is the generic point of the integral scheme $Z_s$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], every nonempty chart $U_i$ has fraction field $\mathcal O_{Z_s,s}$. This is $\kappa(s)$: the closed-immersion map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{Z_s,s}$ is surjective, its target is a field, and hence its kernel is the unique maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{S,s}$; use [def-weil-residue-field]. By the relative-Spec construction in [def-sc-normalization], $\nu_s^{-1}U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with $B_i$ the integral closure of $A_i$ in this fraction field. The ring map $A_i\to B_i$ is integral, so its Spec map is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-integral-ring-map-integral]. Apply [lem-trf-integral-extension-noetherian-spectrum] with the Noetherian domain $A_i$ from Step 1 and the degree-one extension $L=K=\kappa(s)$. It gives Noetherian topology on $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. These finitely many inverse images cover $N_s$; no assertion that $B_i$ is a Noetherian ring or finite over $A_i$ has been made.

source.place: Heinzer, Theorem 2 (printed pp. 371–372) and Corollary (p. 372), the latter being exactly the L=K case used here. Affine normalization via the relative-Spec definition; fraction-field identification via the cited existing node. WANTED: Heinzer PDF absent locally; printed article text read online.

proof.text: For each affine open $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of $S$, the finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives a finite affine cover $f^{-1}W_i=\bigcup_j V_{ij}$ with $V_{ij}=\operatorname{Spec}D_{ij}$ and $D_{ij}$ finitely generated over $R_i$. First form $X_Z=X\times_S Z_s$. Over $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, its affine charts are $V_{ij}\times_{W_i}U_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_{ij}$, where $C_{ij}=D_{ij}\otimes_{R_i}A_i$. Then $X\times_SN_s=X_Z\times_{Z_s}N_s$ has affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}(C_{ij}\otimes_{A_i}B_i)$. These identifications follow from [def-pc-fibre-product]: compatible maps into the affine factors correspond to ring maps out of the tensor product, by its universal property. If $d_1,\ldots,d_n$ generate $D_{ij}$ over $R_i$, then $d_1\otimes1,\ldots,d_n\otimes1$ generate $C_{ij}$ over $A_i$, and their images generate $C_{ij}\otimes_{A_i}B_i$ over $B_i$. Thus these are finitely many finite-type $B_i$-algebra charts covering $X\times_SN_s$.

source.place: Tag 01T1, definition-finite-type; schemes.tex Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes. The tensor universal property and the base-change generators are written out as the elementary argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-noetherian-spectrum] to each finite-type $B_i$-algebra $C_{ij}\otimes_{A_i}B_i$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is Noetherian by Step 2, each affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}(C_{ij}\otimes_{A_i}B_i)$ is Noetherian. There are finitely many such charts and they cover $X\times_SN_s$ by Step 3. Any descending chain of closed subsets restricts to a stationary chain on each chart; take the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices. Beyond it all restrictions, hence the closed subsets themselves, agree. Therefore the whole underlying topological space of $X\times_SN_s$ is Noetherian.

proof.text: A Noetherian topological space is equivalently one in which every nonempty collection of closed subsets has a minimal member under inclusion, by taking complements of ascending chains of open subsets. This is exactly the formulation in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0051, definition-noetherian (descending chain condition for closed subsets). The minimal-member formulation is its equivalent well-founded formulation.
